verifications.claim: The last human moon landing was Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the sixth and most recent time humans have set foot on the Moon'; R2: 'Apollo 17 — the final mission in the program, which was the last time humans traveled to the moon'; R4: 'Apollo 17, the final flight of the program'; R5: 'NASA’s Final Moon Landing Mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Apollo 17 as the final and last human moon landing mission.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 landed on the Moon on December 11, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: NASA astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days exploring the Taurus-Littrow valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Cernan and Schmitt landed in the Taurus–Littrow valley'; 'approximately 75-hour stay on the lunar surface' (75 hours > 72 hours/3 days)
verifications.reasoning: Reference confirms astronauts, location, and duration over three days (75 hours).

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was NASA's final Apollo mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the eleventh and final crewed mission of NASA's Apollo program'; R4: 'Apollo 17, the final flight of the program'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as final Apollo mission.

verifications.claim: The location of the last moon landing was Taurus-Littrow Valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly identifies Taurus-Littrow as the landing site of the last mission.

verifications.claim: The last people on the Moon were Eugene Cernan (Commander) and Harrison Schmitt (Lunar Module Pilot).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Gene Cernan and Lunar Module Pilot Harrison Schmitt walked on the Moon' (final mission)
verifications.reasoning: Names and roles match exactly for the final mission's lunar walkers.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the last to leave the lunar surface on December 14, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Return launch December 14, 1972, 22:54:37 UTC'; 'Cernan then followed Schmitt into the LM'
verifications.reasoning: Date and Cernan as last to enter LM (last to leave surface) confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Apollo 17 crew spent approximately 73 hours on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'longest time on the lunar surface (75 hours)'; 'approximately 75-hour stay'
verifications.reasoning: Reference specifies 75 hours; claim's 'approximately 73' is close but less precise.

verifications.claim: The Apollo 17 crew completed three successful long-duration excursions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Surface EVAs 3'; durations '7 hours, 11 minutes, 53 seconds', etc. (long-duration)

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was the first mission to include a trained scientist (geologist Harrison Schmitt).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Schmitt was the only professional geologist to land on the Moon'; 'first to have a professional geologist'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first mission with a trained geologist (Schmitt).

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 collected the most samples of any Apollo mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'largest lunar-sample return (approximately 115 kg or 254 lb)'; R2: 'gathered more geology samples than any other moon mission, bringing 243 pounds'

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 performed the most experiments of any Apollo mission.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe expanded/new experiments but do not claim or quantify 'most' explicitly.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo program ended with Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the eleventh and final crewed mission of NASA's Apollo program'; R4: 'the final flight of the program'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as ending the Apollo program.
